pending.headline: Study Finds AI Access Makes People Almost Entirely Unwilling to Say 'I Don't Know'

items.title: AI access makes people almost entirely unwilling to say "I don't know," study finds
items.snippet: A study with more than 3,000 participants shows that just having access to AI answers nearly eliminated people's willingness to say "I don't know." In one experiment, it dropped from 44 to 3 percent, even though the AI was almost always wrong. Participants who used AI felt more confident but were correct only about a third as often as those without it. The article AI access makes people almost entirely unwilling to…

pending.summary: A study tracking over 3,000 participants revealed that providing direct access to AI-generated answers nearly eliminated their willingness to admit ignorance. Even when the provided AI responses were incorrect, willingness to say 'I don't know' dropped sharply from 44% to 3%.

items.snippet: SoL-Pi cuts coding agents' token usage by up to 49 percent with little change in performance by optimizing the control layer between the model and its environment. A research agent tested 152 approaches across more than 3,000 runs to develop the system, though the gains were smaller on other benchmarks. pending.summary: Nvidia researchers have introduced SoL-Pi, a control layer optimization that cuts the token consumption of coding agents by up to 49 percent. The approach optimizes communication between models and their execution environments without sacrificing performance.

pending.headline: Researchers Connect GPT-6 Astra Directly to Humanoid Robot to Tidy Kitchen

items.snippet: Researchers from Stanford and Caltech had a humanoid robot powered by GPT-6 Astra independently tidy up an unfamiliar kitchen. Their HomeBody system skips a specially trained control layer, letting the language model call directly into modular skills like grasping and navigating.
